The following diagram shows a triangle ABC.

[Diagram not to scale: A scalene triangle has A at the lower left, B at the upper right and C at the lower right. AC = 15 cm, BC = 10 cm, and the angle ABC at B is θ.]

AC = 15 cm, BC = 10 cm, and ∠ABC = θ.

Let sin ∠CAB = √3/3.

(a) Given that ∠ABC is acute, find sin θ. [3]

(b) Find cos(2 × ∠CAB). [3]
records.independentSolutionText: (a) By the sine rule, sin θ/15 = sin(∠CAB)/10 = (√3/3)/10. Therefore sin θ = 15√3/30 = √3/2. (b) Using cos(2A) = 1 − 2sin²A with sin A = √3/3 gives cos(2A) = 1 − 2(1/3) = 1/3.

Hank sets up a bird table in his garden to provide the local birds with some food. Hank notices
that a specific bird, a large magpie, visits several times per month and he names him Bill. Hank
models the number of times per month that Bill visits his garden as a Poisson distribution with
mean 3.1.
(a)
Using Hank’s model, find the probability that Bill visits the garden on exactly four
occasions during one particular month.
[1]

on exactly 12 occasions.
(ii)
during the first and third month only.
[5]

Bill does not visit the garden.

assumed that each of these baby magpies visits the garden randomly and independently,
and that the number of times each baby magpie visits the garden per month is modelled by
a Poisson distribution with mean 2.1.
(d)
Determine the least number of magpies required, including Bill, in order that the
probability of Hank’s garden having at least 30 magpie visits per month is greater
than 0.2.
[4]

(b) Find the value of k. [2]

(c) Hence, find the value of E(X). [2]
records.independentSolutionText: Successive probabilities halve. (a)(i) a=k/2. (a)(ii) b=k/16. (b) Since P(X=3)=k/4=8/63, k=32/63 (also the six probabilities sum to 1). Thus the probabilities for x=1,…,6 are 32,16,8,4,2,1 divided by 63. (c) E(X)=(32+2·16+3·8+4·4+5·2+6·1)/63=120/63=40/21≈1.90.
